summary: O'Connor pressed ultimate-authorship objections, while Carter defended graded, attributable agency and preserved interpersonal and normative meanings beyond causal explanation.

pro.text: you can do whatever you will you just can't will what you will
pro.context: O'Connor uses the distinction between acting on a want and choosing that want to challenge whether voluntary conduct supplies ultimate control.

con.text: there is a semantic difference between being compelled to act and being freely acting
con.context: Carter grounds compatibilism in the ordinary distinction between compulsion and conduct attributable to the acting person, without requiring action to be uncaused.

move-pro-01-control-dilemma.words: Free will appears to require genuine authorship and an ability to act otherwise, yet determined events inherit prior causes while random events provide no agent-directed control.
move-pro-01-control-dilemma.critique: Strongest feature: The control dilemma establishes the determinist route clearly by placing both causal determination and randomness under one authorship test, while acknowledging that free will is difficult to define precisely. Principal limitation: Its conclusion depends on an approximately specified ability to do otherwise and does not fully justify why philosophical freedom must require ultimate authorship instead of attributable, reasons-responsive voluntary action. Live burden: The argument must explain why compatibilist control is insufficient rather than merely different, and must show that agent-level organization cannot provide relevant control within a determined causal history. Locked score: The strong and competent band fits a foundational, highly relevant dilemma whose intelligible structure and explicit uncertainty are moderated by an underdefended criterion of freedom and limited engagement with the strongest compatibilist alternative.

move-pro-03-causal-regress-of-desire.words: A choice or desire is either random and uncontrolled or determined through a causal chain extending beyond the agent, so neither origin provides ultimate control.
move-pro-03-causal-regress-of-desire.critique: Strongest feature: The causal regress applies the determined-or-random dilemma directly to desires, making the challenge to self-authorship concrete and tightly connected to the determinist route’s central burden. Principal limitation: Its categorical treatment of every mental event compresses possible distinctions between causal dependence, agent-level organization, ownership, and reasons-responsiveness, leaving the universal scope insufficiently qualified. Live burden: The argument must establish that a determined desire cannot constitute a person’s own effective control, rather than assuming that any dependence on antecedent causes eliminates every philosophically relevant freedom. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a coherent, highly responsive regress with clear evidential grounding, while recognizing that its exhaustive framing is somewhat overstated and does not confront the strongest compatibilist distinction between ultimate sourcehood and attributable agency.

move-con-01-attributable-causation.words: Deterministic causation can coexist with freedom because compelled conduct differs meaningfully from voluntary action whose operative cause can be attributed to the acting person.
move-con-01-attributable-causation.critique: Strongest feature: The attributable-causation reply directly accepts causal determination while replacing uncaused authorship with a clear semantic distinction between compelled conduct and action arising from the person. Principal limitation: The criterion for designating a cause as the self remains deliberately approximate, so the move does not fully explain when identification, manipulation, addiction, or internal compulsion defeats attribution. Live burden: The compatibilist account must specify the conditions under which motives genuinely belong to an agent and explain why those conditions answer the determinist demand rather than merely changing the subject. Locked score: The very strong band fits a highly relevant and charitable reframe that contacts both central causal objections, offers a proportionate compatibility claim, and openly acknowledges approximation, despite leaving its operative standard of personal causation somewhat schematic.

move-pro-04-unchosen-wants.words: Conduct follows either force or motivating wants; force plainly defeats control, while acting from wants cannot confer ultimate control when those wants were not themselves chosen.
move-pro-04-unchosen-wants.critique: Strongest feature: The want-or-force reply directly targets attributable causation by distinguishing the ability to act on a desire from the deeper ability to select the desire that governs action. Principal limitation: The dichotomy is stated categorically and treats control over one’s motivating wants as necessary for freedom without independently defending that demanding requirement against reasons-responsive compatibilism. Live burden: The reply must show why acting through an owned, evaluatively integrated motive cannot count as meaningful control unless the agent previously chose or authored that motive. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects excellent contact with the decisive opposing claim, a memorable and recoverable distinction, and clear route relevance, tempered by universal scope, missing qualification, and an assumed connection between unchosen desire and absence of every relevant agency.

move-con-03-degrees-of-voluntariness.words: Ordinary freedom concerns degrees of voluntary control and the presence or absence of practical constraints, not an abstract requirement that agents first choose their desires.
move-con-03-degrees-of-voluntariness.critique: Strongest feature: The graded-voluntariness reply supplies a discriminating practical example, contrasting a suppressible sneeze with an uncontrollable tic to show that meaningful control varies independently of ultimate self-creation. Principal limitation: The example establishes ordinary differences in voluntary capacity but does not demonstrate that such graded control satisfies the determinist’s distinct philosophical demand for ultimate sourcehood. Live burden: The account must connect degrees of behavioral control to a principled standard of freedom and explain why causal antecedents do not undermine the responsibility attached to those degrees. Locked score: The very strong band fits a precise, proportionate, highly responsive reframe that answers the demand for chosen desires with a credible alternative criterion, while preserving the narrower limitation that ordinary voluntariness and ultimate authorship remain separable questions.

move-con-04-undeliberated-voluntary-acti.words: Freedom can admit degrees, and an ordinary voluntary action may belong to an agent even when it was not produced by conscious deliberation or an explicitly willed decision.
move-con-04-undeliberated-voluntary-acti.critique: Strongest feature: The reply usefully separates personal ownership from deliberate manufacture, showing how ordinary voluntary capacities may ground agency even when the operative desire was neither consciously produced nor explicitly willed. Principal limitation: The selected evidence more clearly supports graded control than the distinctive proposition about undeliberated ownership, creating overlap with the neighboring voluntariness move and weakening independent warrant. Live burden: The account must explain which nonconscious or unchosen processes remain attributable to the person and distinguish them from compulsions, implanted motives, or mechanisms that bypass evaluative control. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct contact with the ownership challenge, a plausible and modest compatibilist conclusion, and substantial responsiveness, moderated by partial recoverability and evidence that does not fully display the move’s distinctive inferential step.

move-pro-07-consequentialist-responsibil.words: Abandoning ultimate moral desert does not prevent society from using deterrence, prevention, rehabilitation, or other forward-looking responses to harmful and criminal behavior.
move-pro-07-consequentialist-responsibil.critique: Strongest feature: The consequentialist account clearly preserves practical responses after rejecting ultimate desert, explaining deterrence through competing desires and distinguishing behavioral protection from metaphysical blame. Principal limitation: Demonstrating that prevention and deterrence remain available does not exhaust responsibility, because answerability, recognition, repair, trust, and other interpersonal practices may have independent ethical significance. Live burden: The account must show how its forward-looking framework respects persons and constrains punishment, rather than treating offenders solely as objects to be managed through increasingly powerful incentives. Locked score: The very strong band fits a precise, explicitly qualified, well-warranted answer to a major practical objection, with strong responsiveness and a concrete mechanism, while leaving the compatibilist claim that responsibility includes irreducible interpersonal relations only partially answered.

move-con-07-interpersonal-responsibility.words: Responsibility is an ethically significant interpersonal practice, and freedom is better understood through nuanced recognition of persons than as an absolute metaphysical property.
move-con-07-interpersonal-responsibility.critique: Strongest feature: The interpersonal reframe identifies an important remainder after deterrence, locating freedom and responsibility within practices of recognition, answerability, meaning, and treating another human being as a person. Principal limitation: Terms such as semantic freedom and personal treatment remain elastic, while the asserted ethical indispensability of the framework receives less direct argument than its importance requires. Live burden: The reply must demonstrate why respectful interpersonal practices require the compatibilist label of freedom, since a determinist could preserve dialogue, repair, and recognition while rejecting ultimate desert. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a relevant, charitable, ethically substantial response that broadens the dispute beyond behavioral management, tempered by an incompletely specified criterion and an unresolved question about whether interpersonal meaning establishes freedom or merely coexists with determinism.

move-pro-02-substrate-neutral-dilemma.words: Moving agency into God, a soul, or another immaterial substrate cannot create free control, because any event there remains either determined or not determined.
move-pro-02-substrate-neutral-dilemma.critique: Strongest feature: The substrate-neutral extension consistently applies the same determined-or-undetermined dilemma to souls, God, and immaterial entities, blocking an intuitive escape that merely relocates rather than explains control. Principal limitation: The active compatibilist case does not rely on an immaterial substrate, so defeating theological or dualist alternatives leaves the principal account of attributable voluntary organization substantially untouched. Live burden: The move must connect substrate neutrality to the actual opposing criterion and show why agent-level causation fails whether realized materially or otherwise, instead of answering an unused metaphysical proposal. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects coherent application, clear recoverability, and an appropriately recognized epistemic qualification, balanced against limited responsiveness to the live compatibilist route and the exceptionally strong impossibility claim carried by the general dilemma.

move-pro-08-determinist-compassion.words: Remembering that wrongdoers may not control the factors determining their conduct can encourage greater compassion, forgiveness, understanding, and kindness without denying protective responses.
move-pro-08-determinist-compassion.critique: Strongest feature: The compassion argument offers a concrete ethical benefit of determinism and carefully presents charity as a possible psychological effect rather than an inevitable consequence of accepting causal explanation. Principal limitation: The move supplies a plausible practical association but does not establish how often determinist reflection improves conduct, whether it could also reduce concern for victims, or how compassion should interact with accountability. Live burden: The argument must articulate safeguards that preserve protection, repair, and equal regard while explaining why diminished ultimate blame tends to improve rather than distort interpersonal judgment. Locked score: The strong and competent band fits a well-qualified, accessible, and route-relevant practical consequence grounded directly in the example, with its persuasive force limited by the absence of comparative evidence and a developed institutional or ethical framework.

move-con-08-ethical-tension.words: Ethical judgment should hold together intelligible pictures of responsible choice and causal constraint instead of reducing human agency entirely to either extreme.
move-con-08-ethical-tension.critique: Strongest feature: The ethical-tension proposal captures how moral life can require several intelligible perspectives at once, using the crossroads image to preserve choice without denying causal constraint or human vulnerability. Principal limitation: Its language of pictures and tension remains metaphorical, and retaining multiple descriptions does not itself show that compatibilist freedom is true, coherent, or ethically indispensable. Live burden: The framework must specify when each perspective governs judgment, how conflicts between them are resolved, and why plural description adds more than a determinist account already can retain. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a proportionate, nuanced, and ethically relevant constructive framework with a recoverable central idea, moderated by compressed warrant and the gap between recommending interpretive plurality and establishing the metaphysical or semantic conclusion at issue.

move-pro-09-evolved-moral-desire.words: Moral motivation may arise from evolved emotional desires that compete with other motives and promote cooperation, restraint, and the stability of social groups.
move-pro-09-evolved-moral-desire.critique: Strongest feature: The evolutionary account gives determinism a positive explanation of moral motivation, showing how cooperative desires can emerge and compete with other motives without requiring independently chosen wills. Principal limitation: The compressed passage moves among genes, organisms, societies, intuitions, and desires without clearly separating biological selection, cultural development, motivational psychology, and normative justification. Live burden: The account must clarify its explanatory level and show how evolutionary causation relates to moral authority, while avoiding the stronger claim that causal origins exhaust the meaning of moral judgment. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a relevant, plausible, and cautiously expressed account of cooperative motivation, tempered by shifting explanatory levels, limited comparison with cultural alternatives, and no developed answer to the distinction between explaining why moral feelings occur and justifying them.

move-con-09-normative-nonreduction.words: A psychological or evolutionary explanation of moral intuition may identify its causes without eliminating or fully capturing the intuition’s richer normative content and meaning.
move-con-09-normative-nonreduction.critique: Strongest feature: The nonreduction reply precisely distinguishes causal psychological motivation from the richer normative concept of moral intuition, directly diagnosing why an origin story need not settle meaning or authority. Principal limitation: The objection defeats only an exhaustive or debunking interpretation, while the determinist account may have intended merely to explain motivation without eliminating independent normative discourse. Live burden: The reply must identify what additional normative content survives causal explanation and explain how that content supports agency or freedom rather than simply marking a conceptual distinction. Locked score: The very strong band fits a clear, carefully qualified, and highly responsive diagnostic challenge that preserves evolutionary facts while resisting reduction, with its reach properly limited because it does not refute the narrower causal explanation or independently establish moral freedom.

move-pro-05-unchosen-source-regress.words: Choices reflect unchosen upbringing, genetics, circumstances, and dispositions, so tracing their causal source backward never reaches an agent who created the conditions of agency.
move-pro-05-unchosen-source-regress.critique: Strongest feature: The source regress concretely traces conduct through upbringing, parents, genetics, circumstances, and conformity, challenging both personal attribution and local degrees of control as final explanations of authorship. Principal limitation: Its claim about all human behavior and identical outcomes under duplicated conditions is universal and insufficiently qualified, extending beyond what the herd analogy or selected counterfactual establishes. Live burden: The reply must distinguish ultimate origination from relevant personal sourcehood and explain why an agent cannot count as a source merely because the agent was not self-created. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a recognizable, centrally relevant challenge that contacts major compatibilist claims, but whose materially overstated scope, partial response to normative nonreduction, and failure to defeat attributable sourcehood prevent the regress from carrying its intended conclusion fully.

move-con-05-reflexive-first-person-persp.words: Disclosing a prediction to a self-aware subject may provoke its defeat, suggesting a reflexive first-person perspective not captured by ordinary third-person causal prediction.
move-con-05-reflexive-first-person-persp.critique: Strongest feature: The first-person proposal identifies a genuine complication for prediction by emphasizing reflexivity, existential self-interpretation, and the possibility that disclosed information changes the behavior being predicted. Principal limitation: The selected evidence only partially recovers the distinctive prediction-defeat proposition and does not show that reflexive responses escape determination rather than becoming further causes within it. Live burden: The reply must provide a visible mechanism connecting self-reference to agency and directly answer why upbringing, genetics, and antecedent conditions cannot determine the subject’s response to disclosure. Locked score: The mixed band fits relevant and cautiously expressed first-person material with philosophical promise, while recognizing weak contact with the decisive causal-source demands, partial proposition recoverability, and an unresolved inference from epistemic difficulty in prediction to metaphysical or practical freedom.

move-con-02-mediopassive-agency.words: An action may genuinely belong to a person while also happening to that person, without requiring deliberate manufacture of every underlying thought, desire, or process.
move-con-02-mediopassive-agency.critique: Strongest feature: The mediopassive model supplies a coherent category in which an event can be both something a person does and something done to that person, directly reframing self-manufacture. Principal limitation: The marriage and grammatical examples establish conceptual possibility but do not determine which ordinary actions possess the relevant dual structure or when passive influence overwhelms genuine ownership. Live burden: The account must formulate criteria for mediopassive attribution and explain why this relation answers the ultimate-source objection rather than preserving only an ordinary sense of belonging. Locked score: The very strong band reflects a precise, memorable, proportionate, and highly responsive reframe that contacts several decisive determinist claims, with only a bounded residual gap between demonstrating attributable ownership and refuting the distinct demand for ultimate authorship.

move-pro-06-introspective-mechanism-gap.words: People can initiate voluntary movement while lacking introspective access to how wanting or deciding produces the bodily action, as illustrated by intentionally moving a finger.
move-pro-06-introspective-mechanism-gap.critique: Strongest feature: The introspective example clearly contrasts awareness of bodily mechanics with the puzzling immediacy of intentionally moving a finger, raising a legitimate question about access to action initiation. Principal limitation: Limited introspective access does not by itself establish absence of agency, and the selected evidence only partially recovers the proposed gap between wanting, deciding, and bodily movement. Live burden: The observation must connect its epistemic limitation to an eligible route requirement or opposing claim and explain why unavailable mechanism-level awareness matters for control rather than merely for self-knowledge. Locked score: The mixed band fits a coherent, appropriately exploratory, and experientially grounded diagnostic question, while its lack of direct burden contact, partial recoverability, and missing inference from introspective opacity to diminished freedom sharply constrain its argumentative contribution.

move-con-06-public-first-consciousness.words: Conscious thought may be socially and behaviorally constituted before private representation, so reductive inner inspection cannot isolate it as a discrete, self-contained object.
move-con-06-public-first-consciousness.critique: Strongest feature: The public-first account offers meaningful adjacent evidence about consciousness, using pain behavior and feedback loops to challenge a simplistic picture of thought as an exclusively private internal object. Principal limitation: The move shifts between behavioral evidence, semantic constitution, and metaphysical priority, while failing to explain the mechanism connecting voluntary intention to bodily movement that the opposing example raises. Live burden: The reply must distinguish public evidence of experience from constitution of experience and show how social feedback answers either introspective opacity or the deeper regress through unchosen causes. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a recoverable, relevant, and philosophically suggestive thesis, moderated by unstable terminology, underdefended priority, and its classification as a relevant nonanswer to both decisive targets identified in the exchange.

strengths: The determined-or-random dilemma and its application to desires supplied a consistent, substrate-neutral challenge to ultimate authorship across the debate.
The want-or-force reply directly contacted the compatibilist attribution standard by asking whether ownership of action suffices when motivating wants remain unchosen.
The practical case preserved deterrence, prevention, rehabilitation, and compassion without relying on ultimate moral desert, answering a prominent ethical concern.
The source regress concretely connected choices to upbringing, genetics, circumstances, and dispositions, keeping the deepest authorship question visible despite later overstatement.

blunders.text: The determinist case sometimes moved from the absence of ultimate self-creation to the absence of every relevant kind of control without separately defending that broader conclusion.

tags.label: Begging the question
tags.context: The inference risks assuming that genuine freedom already requires ultimate authorship, which is the central standard disputed by the compatibilist account.

blunders.text: The source-regress argument generalized from upbringing, genetics, and conformity to all human behavior and an exact same-conditions outcome without adequate qualification.

tags.label: Scope neglect
tags.context: The universal conclusion exceeds the scale and specificity of the examples offered, which support causal influence more readily than exhaustive behavioral determination.

strengths: The attributable-causation distinction directly answered the opening dilemma while accepting determinism, providing a clear criterion based on compulsion and personal sourcehood.
The sneeze-and-tic comparison gave the strongest concrete account of graded voluntariness and showed why ordinary control need not require choosing every desire.
The mediopassive model offered a memorable conceptual structure for actions that belong to persons while also arising through processes they did not manufacture.
The interpersonal and normative replies preserved dimensions of responsibility and moral meaning that a purely causal or deterrence-centered description did not exhaust.

blunders.text: The first-person prediction proposal did not clearly establish its distinctive mechanism or answer why reflexive behavior could not itself remain determined by disclosed information.

tags.label: Argument from ignorance
tags.context: Difficulty predicting a self-aware subject cannot establish nondetermination without positive support connecting reflexive prediction failure to freedom or causal independence.

blunders.text: The public-first consciousness reply shifted among behavioral evidence, semantic constitution, and metaphysical priority, leaving the original mechanism question substantially unanswered.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: The senses of public and private move between observable evidence, social formation, and the location or constitution of conscious experience.

tags.label: Red herring
tags.context: The adjacent discussion of pain behavior and social feedback diverts from the specific challenge about how intention produces voluntary bodily movement.

thesis.text: The strongest determinist thesis is not that determined people lack all practical agency, but that no person ultimately authors the inherited conditions that make deliberation, character, and action occur; therefore practices requiring basic, backward-looking desert need independent justification.

novelty.explanation: This narrows the live claim from denial of every useful control capacity to denial of ultimate authorship and basic desert.

premises.text: Randomness cannot provide authorship because an event’s lack of determination does not make its occurrence controlled, selected, or intelligibly attributable to an agent as its ultimate creator.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript’s randomness branch while stating precisely why indeterminacy alone cannot create ultimate control.

premises.text: Determined deliberation can remain responsive, intelligent, and personally attributable, yet its evaluative standards, capacities, and initial motivational economy still arise from conditions the deliberating person did not ultimately choose.

novelty.explanation: This concedes graded and attributable agency while preserving the narrower challenge concerning ultimate sourcehood.

premises.text: The regress need not claim that every cause lies outside the organism; it needs only show that tracing the formation of the agent’s reasons and dispositions never reaches a self-created foundation.

novelty.explanation: This corrects the overbroad universal framing and distinguishes internal personal causation from ultimate self-creation.

premises.text: Forward-looking responsibility can preserve protection, deterrence, rehabilitation, restitution, dialogue, and interpersonal recognition while withholding suffering imposed solely because an offender supposedly deserves it in an ultimate sense.

novelty.explanation: This expands the practical account to answer the objection that consequential responsibility treats persons merely as manageable objects.

premises.text: A causal explanation of moral motivation need not reduce normative meaning; it can explain how agents become sensitive to reasons while leaving open separate questions about which reasons are sound.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the evolutionary account by withdrawing any exhaustive reduction of moral judgment to psychological desire.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, determined agents may exercise meaningful local control and participate in ethical relationships, but those facts do not establish ultimate self-authorship or basic desert; responsibility should therefore be justified through protective, reparative, communicative, and rehabilitative purposes.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion integrates the strongest compatibilist concessions while retaining a proportionate rejection of ultimate desert.

newArguments.title: Moral luck symmetry
newArguments.text: If two agents form the same harmful intention but external luck permits only one to complete the harm, ordinary blame often differs dramatically even though the agential inputs were comparable. Similar luck affects temperament, opportunity, upbringing, and exposure to corrective reasons. A responsibility system sensitive to this symmetry should hesitate before treating outcomes or inherited character as grounds for basic desert. It can still distinguish risk, intention, harm, and future danger for protection and repair, but those distinctions justify tailored responses rather than the claim that anyone ultimately created the self from which the conduct issued.

novelty.explanation: The transcript packet contains no locked move developing moral luck as an independent argument against basic desert.

newArguments.title: Institutional burden of justification
newArguments.text: Coercive institutions need not resolve every metaphysical question before acting, but they should justify each imposed burden by a public purpose that the burden can plausibly advance. Prevention, rehabilitation, restitution, and proportionate deterrence can meet that test; suffering imposed only to express ultimate desert cannot appeal to the same forward-looking evidence. This shifts the practical burden: uncertainty about self-authorship counsels restraint where punishment has no protective, reparative, or communicative function. The argument does not abolish responsibility; it requires institutions to connect responsibility practices to defensible human purposes.

novelty.explanation: This develops the practical determinist route into a public standard for constraining coercive punishment.

thesis.text: The strongest compatibilist thesis defines freedom as a graded capacity to govern conduct through reasons, values, and substantially uncoerced deliberative mechanisms that belong to the person, without requiring the impossible achievement of creating oneself from nothing.

novelty.explanation: This converts the approximate attribution account into a more explicit reasons-responsive and graded criterion of personal agency.

premises.text: Causal determination does not erase functional differences between conduct produced through an agent’s evaluative capacities and conduct produced by threats, seizures, manipulation, or compulsions that bypass those capacities.

novelty.explanation: This develops the compulsion distinction into a criterion based on whether normal evaluative capacities govern action.

premises.text: An action belongs to a person when it issues from mechanisms integrated with that person’s values and capable of adjusting across a suitable range of reasons, even though those mechanisms have causal histories.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the missing conditions for designating an operative cause as the acting person.

premises.text: Freedom is therefore scalar: coercion, addiction, ignorance, developmental immaturity, cognitive impairment, and available alternatives can diminish control in different ways without making all agency disappear whenever causation is present.

novelty.explanation: This generalizes the graded sneeze-and-tic example into a broader context-sensitive account of impaired agency.

premises.text: Ultimate self-creation is unnecessary for authorship because authorship ordinarily concerns whether present conduct expresses and is governed by the person’s operative capacities, not whether the person created every condition enabling them.

novelty.explanation: This directly answers the source regress instead of relying only on ordinary attribution or grammatical illustration.

premises.text: Interpersonal responsibility can recognize causal vulnerability while still asking agents for reasons, inviting repair, revising trust, and responding proportionately to the degree of control actually exercised.

novelty.explanation: This explains the practical content of interpersonal responsibility and incorporates the determinist concern about humane restraint.

conclusion.text: Thus, determinism is compatible with a meaningful but limited freedom whenever conduct flows through the person’s reasons-responsive capacities without decisive coercion or bypass, supporting graded responsibility while excluding claims of absolute independence from causal history.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion states a bounded compatibility claim and answers the demand for clearer criteria of attribution and responsibility.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual reasons profile
newArguments.text: Relevant freedom can be tested without asking whether the entire past could remain identical. Ask instead whether the agent’s decision mechanism would respond appropriately across nearby situations in which reasons, evidence, or stakes differed. A coerced, compulsive, or bypassed mechanism has a restricted response profile; a deliberative mechanism can register considerations, revise intentions, and learn. Determinism is compatible with those counterfactual differences because each nearby situation includes different inputs. This account explains why control varies and supplies an operational distinction between personal governance and mere causal transmission.

novelty.explanation: No locked transcript move develops counterfactual sensitivity to reasons as an independent test of compatibilist control.

newArguments.title: Diachronic self-governance
newArguments.text: Agency is not confined to the instant when a desire appears. People shape future conduct by forming habits, avoiding temptations, seeking information, making commitments, requesting treatment, and arranging environments that support endorsed aims. None of these activities requires self-creation, yet together they allow a person to govern how later motives become effective. This diachronic perspective answers the objection that one cannot simply choose a present want: freedom may consist partly in the temporally extended capacity to evaluate motives and influence which dispositions guide future action.

novelty.explanation: This extends graded voluntariness into a temporally extended account that directly addresses the inability to choose an immediate desire.
